title: Radiographic cup position following hip arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial protocol
author: Christine Kruse
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jpbcmin
materials: We hypothesized that PA would have a larger anteversion and inclination and that LA would have a larger FO and AM postoperatively than PA. Furthermore, we hypothesized that we would have a high inter and intra reliability (ICC>0.81) of our measurements.
Patients scheduled for primary cementless total hip arthroplasty

steps.title: Patient Recruitment and Randomization
steps.instruction: Recruit patients from the outpatient clinic and assign them to a surgical approach group.

substeps.instruction: Screen patients based on inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., endstage primary hip OA or secondary OA with CE angle >20 degrees; exclude those with severe medical conditions or inability to walk 20m without aid).
Obtain written and oral informed consent.
Assign participants to either Posterior Approach (PA) or Lateral Approach (LA) using a random computer-generated sequence via sealed envelopes handled by a nurse.

steps.title: Surgical Intervention
steps.instruction: Perform total hip arthroplasty (THA) using cementless components (Bi-metric stem® and Exceed ABT Ringloc-x Shell™) with the patient in lateral decubitus position.

substeps.instruction: For Posterior Approach (PA): Make a curved incision over the posterior greater trochanter, dissect gluteus maximus, detach external rotators, and incise the posterior hip capsule. Dislocate hip via internal rotation and flexion. Perform capsular repair and re-insert external rotators during closure.

For Lateral Approach (LA): Make a midline incision over the greater trochanter, detach the anterior one-third of gluteus medius and gluteus minimus insertions. Excise the hip capsule on the anterior side from the collum femoris basis to the acetabular rim. Dislocate hip via external rotation, adduction, and flexion. Re-insert gluteus medius and minimus during closure (no capsular repair).
Close all wounds with nylon suture.

steps.title: Radiographic Image Acquisition
steps.instruction: Obtain pre- and postoperative AP radiographs of the pelvis following a standard protocol.

substeps.instruction: Position patient supine with 15 degrees bilateral internal rotation of the hip joint.
Center the X-ray beam over the symphysis pubis joint.

steps.title: Image Processing and Calibration
steps.instruction: Import radiographs from web-PACS into TraumaCad® and calibrate for size using a high-resolution diagnostic screen (Fa. WIDE type 2103 CP).

substeps.instruction: Calibrate preoperative radiographs using a 25.4mm calibration marker ball.
Calibrate postoperative radiographs using the known size of the implanted metal head.

steps.title: Radiographic Quality Screening
steps.instruction: Filter radiographs based on pre-defined inclusion criteria to ensure measurement quality.

substeps.instruction: Verify Tönnis foramen obturator index (FOI) is between 0.7-1.8 (calculated as maximum horizontal width of right obturator foramen divided by width of left).
Ensure full visibility of the greater and lesser trochanters, and both femurs 2.5 cm distal to the lesser trochanter.
Confirm detectable radiographic teardrops.

steps.title: Measure Cup Position
steps.instruction: Measure anteversion and inclination on postoperative radiographs based on the coronal plane.

substeps.instruction: Measure Anteversion: Use the 'Cup Version' option in TraumaCad® (Lewinnek's method), defining the long axis as the cup diameter and the short axis as the longest perpendicular line from the anterior to posterior rim.

Measure Inclination: Calculate the angle between a horizontal line connecting the two most inferior parts of the ischial tuberosities and the line of the cup's long axis (drawn through the most lateral/superior and most inferior/medial points).

steps.title: Measure Offset and Leg Length
steps.instruction: Measure the following parameters on both pre- and postoperative radiographs.

substeps.instruction: Femoral Offset (FO): Perpendicular distance from the center of rotation (COR) of the femoral head to the center axis of the femur.
Cup Offset (CO): Horizontal distance from the COR to the vertical tangent of Koehler’s teardrop’s lateral side.
Total Offset (TO): Sum of FO and CO.

Abduction Moment Arm (AM): Length of a straight line from the COR to a perpendicular point of the tangent of the greater trochanter (tangent drawn between the most lateral spot of the most superior part and the most inferior spot of the most lateral point).
Leg Length: Draw a horizontal line between the two acetabular teardrops and measure the perpendicular vertical distance from this line to the most prominent points on the lesser trochanters.

steps.title: Reliability and Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Evaluate the consistency of measurements and analyze the data.

substeps.instruction: Perform intraobserver reliability check: One author (CK) measures 20 random patients twice with a two-week interval.
Perform interobserver reliability check: Three authors (CK, SR, LB) independently measure the same 20 random patients.
Calculate Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) using a two-way mixed-effects model with absolute agreement (ICC >0.81 considered excellent).
Analyze group differences using unpaired t-tests for means/standard deviations and chi-squared tests for the number of cups outside the safe zone.

description: The statistical significance level was set at p<0.05. The statistics was performed using STATA version 13.1 (StataCorp LP, TX, USA).
